outlook.statement: The company's turnover has increased manifold over time and is expected to grow substantially in subsequent years.
Looking ahead, we aim to expand our distribution network, explore new product categories, and invest in technology to enhance productivity and sustainability.
The Indian edible oil industry is well-positioned to tap into its strong growth potential while managing emerging risks.

risks: Majority of raw material comes from imports; geo-political events can cause supply disruptions, exporting countries government can put restrictions on exports.
Weather conditions can result in reduction of crop production.
Operational factors include operating efficiency, product diversity, market position, ability to secure raw material, commodity price and forex-risk management systems.
Risk financial position and returns metrics, capital structure, ability to generate positive cash flows from operations and adequacy in relation to contractual debt service obligations.
Increase in taxes on import of crude edible oil; restriction on quantity that any Company can import.
Exposed to commodity price fluctuations; edible oil prices in India directly correlated to international oil price movements and currency movements.
Risks broadly classified into Strategic Risk, Compliance and Governance Risk, Financial Risk, Environmental Risk, Operational Risk and Social Risk.
Key risks for edible oils sector include change in import-export regulations; change in minimum support price (MSP) on oilseeds; high dependence on monsoons; exchange rate fluctuations.
Increase in number of competing brands, counter campaigning and aggressive pricing by competitors.
Changing consumer preference and demand; shift in consumer preferences induced by pandemic; speed of shift via social media.
Profitability significantly influenced by regulatory changes; highly susceptible to changes in duty differential between import duties on crude and refined oil by Government of India.
Profitability depends on changes in export tax levied by exporting countries, mainly Indonesia and Malaysia (account for most of palm oil imports).
Revenue recognition and year-end cut-off risk due to high volume of transactions, pricing volatility in edible oil industry, and inherent risk of management override

Inventory valuation and process loss estimation risk due to significant management judgment in determination of cost, allocation of production overheads, estimation of process loss and yield, and assessment of net realizable value considering volatility in edible oil prices
